answer: A proof-of-space-time protocol requires each agent to commit dedicated storage across an orchard of local drives. Each identity must sustain an ongoing vine of cryptographic challenge proofs, imposing the verifiable hardware cost of uncompressed disk capacity per fabricated node. Gateways refract response timings through an auditing prism to prevent storage outsourcing. However, persistent proof cycles accelerate drive degradation and exclude storage-constrained agents.
